v.why: The L2 term is divided by batch size, so tiny batches feel a much stronger effective penalty and over-regularize.
Narrow nets have little spare capacity, so extra shrinkage pushes them into underfitting.
Deeper unnormalized ReLU nets need many updates in a fixed epoch budget and large batches give few steps.
Depth supplies representational capacity that a narrow net lacks.
Deeper unnormalized ReLU nets are more prone to divergence and dead units at near-divergent learning rates.
More units give a larger output change per Adam step, which speeds up an undertrained tiny-lr run.
Strong L2 shrinks the added units toward zero, so the capacity is cancelled and the net is over-regularized.
Fewer updates from larger batches hurt most when a tiny learning rate already leaves the net undertrained.
Larger batches average out gradient noise and keep near-divergent training from collapsing.
Large batches give few updates and smooth gradients, so a larger step size compensates and is safe.
